text.p: Bonds ended well-supported even if the long end did not fully follow the afternoon rally of the Spanish market. But the spread with the German bunds stands around a historic low of 95 basis points.
Traders saw the spread with Spain at the long end returning to between zero and minus five basis points from its plus two basis point close on Friday.
Dealers saw the shorter end, the three to five year sector, having the greatest potential for gain due to the prospects for further interest rate cuts in Portugal.
They said the 20 basis point cut in the repurchase pact rate on Friday reflected the strength of the escudo and did not exhaust the Bank of Portugal's room to lower money rates.
"Despite the cut, the escudo remains strong. It is expected that the (December) inflation figures confirm the downward (prices) trend and Spain should cut soon, too."
"In other words, a further cut in Portugal can be expected in the coming weeks, and one has to think in further gains in the bonds up to five years," said one trader.
The escudo closed strong against the mark at 99.56/61 to the German currency after closing at 99.90/93 on Thursday.
